headline: Serbia's longtime leader admits defeat to students

sources.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to student-led movement in parliamentary elections (RTE, Reuters)
Vucic Concedes Serbia Election Defeat as Student List Claims 135-140 Seats (Novinite)
Serbia holds parliamentary election as populist leader Vucic faces student movement (France 24)

chunks.text: Serbia held an early parliamentary election on October 25, 2026. Voters {{showed up}} in large numbers, and news reports said [[turnout]] was the highest since 1992. That evening, the country's longtime leader [[admitted defeat]]. He said a list backed by the student protest movement had won. He added that the [[final results]] were not ready. Celebrations soon {{broke out}} in Belgrade and other cities. Drivers [[honked their horns]] as young people [[chanted]] "Victory!"

verbs.correct: To come to a place to take part
verbs.wrong: To send a vote by mail
verbs.why: Most of the class shows up early on test days. Few people show up for the game when it rains. Voters showed up in large numbers on October 25, 2026.

verbs.wrong: To be held in a big stadium
verbs.why: Laughter often breaks out in her class. Applause breaks out when the home team scores. Celebrations broke out in Belgrade and other cities that evening.

chunks.text: The leader's numbers came from a [[sample]] of [[polling stations]], not a [[full count]]. He said the student-led list would win 135 to 140 of the 250 [[seats]] in parliament. He expected his own list to win about 105. The first official [[figures]] {{came in}} from only about 200 polling stations and showed his side ahead. A list needs 126 seats to [[govern]] alone. If his [[estimate]] is correct, the student-led list could {{take over}} the government.

verbs.wrong: To be checked a second time
verbs.why: Orders come in all day at the pizza shop. Votes from small towns come in slowly. The first official figures came in from only about 200 polling stations.
A new principal takes over the school when the old one retires. Big companies often take over smaller ones. If his estimate is correct, the student-led list could take over the government.

chunks.text: Earlier that day, the leader said his side would accept the [[will of the voters]] if it lost. Later, he said his party would {{carry on}} fighting as the [[opposition]]. The student movement asked [[supporters]] to stay calm. It told them to {{stay away}} from areas with many police officers. It also asked people to help watch the count. The list says it wants to {{crack down on}} [[corruption]] and improve schools.

verbs.why: She carries on with her work after the baby falls asleep. The band carries on playing during the storm. The leader said his party would carry on fighting as the opposition.

verbs.correct: To not go near a place
verbs.why: Small children stay away from the hot stove. Many people stay away from busy stores on weekends. The student movement told supporters to stay away from areas with many police officers.

verbs.correct: To act strongly to stop something
verbs.why: The city cracks down on drivers who speed near schools. Many teachers crack down on cheating during exams. The student-led list says it wants to crack down on corruption.

chunks.text: Official results from the election commission {{come out}} in the days after the vote. Then the new parliament must meet and vote on a prime minister. Forming a new government can {{drag on}} for weeks. On election night, the list had not {{put forward}} a [[candidate]] for prime minister. On October 20, its leader, a [[heart doctor]], said the list had more than one candidate for every job. Serbians will then {{find out}} who leads their next government.

verbs.wrong: To be kept in a safe place
verbs.why: Test scores come out every summer. The new job numbers come out each Friday. Official results from the election commission come out in the days after the vote.

verbs.correct: To last longer than people want
verbs.wrong: To be shown on live television
verbs.why: Some work meetings drag on for hours. In some years, the cold weather drags on into April. Forming a new government in Serbia can drag on for weeks.

verbs.correct: To name someone as a choice for a job
verbs.wrong: To thank someone for their hard work
verbs.why: Each party puts forward a candidate for mayor. The coach puts forward two players for team captain. On election night, the list had not put forward a candidate for prime minister.
Students find out their grades online. Most people find out the news on their phones. Serbians will then find out who leads their next government.

mainIdea.s: Serbia's longtime leader said a student-led list won the October 25 vote, using early figures. Official results come first, and then the new parliament will choose a prime minister.
mainIdea.why: The leader admitted defeat on election night. Official results come out in the days after the vote, and forming a government can drag on for weeks.

mainIdea.s: Serbia's election commission announced on election night that a student-led list had won a full majority. Its supporters expect a new government to start work within a few days.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the claim came from the leader's own sample, not the election commission. Forming a government can drag on for weeks.

mainIdea.s: Thousands of university students marched to Belgrade to ask for lower fees and better classrooms. Many teachers joined them, and some schools around the country closed for a week.
mainIdea.why: This story is about an election. The longtime leader admitted defeat, and celebrations broke out in Belgrade.

tf.s: Serbia's longtime leader admitted defeat on election night.
tf.why: He said a student-led list had won, and celebrations broke out in Belgrade soon after.

tf.s: Very few voters showed up for the election.
tf.why: Voters showed up in large numbers, and turnout was the highest since 1992.

tf.s: The leader's figures came from a sample, not a full count.
tf.why: He said the final results were not ready yet. Official results from the election commission come out in the days after the vote.

tf.s: The leader said his party would leave parliament after the vote.
tf.why: He said his party would carry on fighting as the opposition in parliament.

tf.s: The leader expected the student-led list to win most of the seats.
tf.why: He said it would win 135 to 140 of 250 seats, so it could take over the government alone.

tf.s: The student movement told supporters to go to areas with many police.
tf.why: The student movement asked supporters to stay calm and to stay away from areas with many police officers.

lines.text: Did you see the news from Serbia? Celebrations {{broke out}} in Belgrade on election night.
I saw the pictures. What happened?
The country's longtime leader admitted defeat. He said a student-led list won.
Wow. Is that the final result?
Not yet. His numbers came from a sample of polling stations, not a full count.
Right. [[First things first]], the official results need to {{come out}}.
Did a lot of people vote?
Yes. Voters {{showed up}} in huge numbers. Turnout was the highest since 1992.
If his numbers are right, could the student-led list {{take over}} the government?
It could. He expected the list to get more than the 126 seats it needs.
The job is still [[up for grabs]]. On election night, the list hadn't {{put forward}} a candidate.
I guess everyone just has to [[sit tight]].
Yes. Forming a government can {{drag on}} for weeks.
And what does his party say?
He said it would {{carry on}} fighting as the opposition.
Either way, a lot of young voters see this as [[a fresh start]].
